slides: More circle tools. These two tools show up in the hardest circle questions, near the end of the section. And right after this lesson, two questions teach two more tools.

slides.say: The first tool. Two equal circles, and each one passes through the center of the other. Here's a circle with center O, and an equal circle with center P. P is on the first circle, and O is on the second one.
at: Here's a circle with center O

slides.say: The circles cross at two points, A and B. What can we say about this shape? No angle is given, so we add helper lines. We join the centers to the crossing points.
at: The circles cross at two points

slides.say: O A and O B are radii of the first circle. P A and P B are radii of the second circle. And O P? P is on the first circle, so O P is also a radius. The circles are equal, so all five lines have the same length, r.
at: so O P is also a radius

slides.say: So triangle O A P has three equal sides. It's equilateral, and triangle O B P is equilateral too. Every angle in them is sixty degrees.
Now the angle A O B. It's sixty plus sixty, a hundred twenty degrees. And a hundred twenty degrees is a third of the circle, because three times a hundred twenty is three hundred sixty.
Questions love the region the two circles share, the shape in the middle. Draw the chord A B. It cuts this shape into two equal pieces.

Look at the right piece. It's between the chord A B and an arc of the circle with center O. Take the sector A O B, a third of that circle. Then take away triangle A O B. What's left is exactly the right piece.
The left piece is the same, in the circle with center P. So the shared region is two times, the sector minus the triangle.
Let's see it in numbers. Say the radius is six. The whole circle is pi times six squared, thirty-six pi. The sector A O B is a third of it, so it's twelve pi.

Now triangle A O B. The four radii make a rhombus, O A P B. Let's take it out. O P cuts it into our two equilateral triangles. Remember, the area of every equilateral triangle is a squared, times root three, over four. Six squared is thirty-six, and thirty-six over four is nine, so each one is nine root three.

Now cut the same rhombus the other way, with the chord A B. A diagonal cuts a rhombus into two equal halves, and triangle A O B is one of them. So it's half of the rhombus, the same as one equilateral triangle, nine root three.
So one piece is twelve pi minus nine root three. The shared region is two pieces, twenty-four pi minus eighteen root three.
at: The shared region is two pieces

slides.say: The second tool is a ring. Two circles with the same center, O, and the ring between them. The ring is the big circle minus the small circle, pi R squared minus pi r squared.
at: Two circles with the same center
The ring is the big circle

slides.say: Now a chord A B of the big circle that just touches the small circle, at the point M. M is a point of tangency, so the automatic helper line is the radius O M. It's perpendicular to the chord.

Draw O A and O B too. They're radii of the big circle, so triangle A O B is isosceles. O M is the height to its base, and in an isosceles triangle that height is also a median. So M cuts the chord in half. Call each half h.
at: Draw O A and O B
So M cuts the chord in half

slides.say: Look at the right triangle O M B. Its legs are r and h, and its hypotenuse is R. By Pythagoras, r squared plus h squared is R squared. So R squared minus r squared is h squared.
And the ring? Pi R squared minus pi r squared is pi times, R squared minus r squared. That's pi times h squared. So the ring depends only on the chord.
So if the chord is ten, then h is five, and the ring is twenty-five pi. We don't need either radius.
at: So if the chord is ten

slides.say: Let's check it on rings with a chord of ten. Radii twelve and thirteen, the five, twelve, thirteen triangle. A hundred sixty-nine pi minus a hundred forty-four pi is twenty-five pi.
Radii five and five root two, a silver triangle with legs five and five. Five root two, squared, is fifty. Fifty pi minus twenty-five pi is twenty-five pi again.
at: Radii five and five root two

slides.say: And if the small circle shrinks to a single point? Then the chord is a diameter of ten, and the ring is a whole circle with radius five, twenty-five pi. The same answer.
So when a chord of the big circle touches the small circle, the ring is pi times half the chord, squared. Now let's see the other two tools in questions. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next video.
